situation.roe_position: The return on equity is very high because Heritage is a Florida-weighted coastal property insurer in a benign stretch. Rate increases, Florida litigation reform, a lower reinsurance bill and favourable reserve releases have pushed the combined ratio to the low 70s, and the base-year equity is small. It was loss-making in 2021 and 2022 and earned a 94.2% combined ratio in 2024. The current level reflects a light catastrophe run and reserve releases that management says will fade, so I expect a step down toward a mid-teens or lower ROE.
situation.why: The 2025 ROE of 0.67 sits on equity rebuilt from 131.0M in 2022 and is not a normal level. Nearly all premium is coastal, so one severe season could wipe out several years of earnings. Book growth is limited more by management's choice to return capital through buybacks than by a shortage of regulatory capital. Year-end statutory surplus was 392.5M against 505.3M of GAAP equity, and the packet gives no current surplus or dividend capacity, so I rate the constraint as unclear.

situation.roe_position: The 2025 return on opening equity of 0.6726 and the current 36% annualized ROE are inflated by peak conditions. Catastrophe losses are light, Florida litigation reform has cut claim costs, rates are adequate, reinsurance now costs less, and reserve releases are large ($14.0M in Q3 alone). The record also shows a long loss history (-0.45 in 2022, -0.17 in 2021) before the turn. Management says reserve releases will moderate, and the book is nearly all coastal, so a normal cat year would lower returns. Equity is also still small relative to earnings, which flatters the ratio.
situation.why: Statutory surplus of the three insurance subsidiaries was $392.5M at year-end 2025, against net premiums earned of roughly $0.8B, so regulatory capital and rating agencies likely limit how much can be paid out. The evidence gives no current surplus or dividend capacity. Buybacks are modest ($50M authorized for 2027), so book equity will keep compounding fast and growth sits above ROE-supportable payout until returns normalize. Heavy cat and reserve risk argues for retaining capital.
